title: Optional bounded LAN compatibility bridge
facts: Normal Arch-native startup creates no TCP listener; the production LAN bridge is started only by an explicit typed command.
The bridge binds only a selected detected RFC1918/link-local IPv4 address on a random high port, enforces TTL/attempt/header/body limits, and auto-closes after one authenticated request.
The p2p-kanban-lan-bridge/1 envelope uses XChaCha20-Poly1305 with a 256-bit one-time capability and fixed POST/path AAD.

A fresh secp256k1/BIP340 native device keypair is generated locally at bridge start; only the public key crosses IPC and private identity material is consumed through the existing A11 SecretVault provisioning path.
The WebView keeps zero generic permissions and connect-src none; no firewall, mDNS, systemd, shell, file or general HTTP API is added.
inferences: A temporary encrypted compatibility wrapper can close the legacy LAN enrollment gap without reintroducing the permanent backend/server deployment model.
Requiring durable SecretVault before activation avoids committing an imported profile whose device/board secrets disappear on restart.
proposals: Remove rather than expand this bridge once all supported clients can complete native device-link provisioning without the legacy LAN wrapper.
Keep physical legacy-client interoperability as explicit multi-client evidence rather than silently widening the native endpoint set.
unresolved: Representative Android/web legacy-client pairing against the final wrapper still requires physical/cross-client evidence.
User-facing QR rendering is not implemented; the typed UI exposes endpoint, fresh public key and one-time capability for copy/scan tooling without adding a QR/network dependency.
